assertions.claim: GitHub Copilot is shifting from a request-based pricing model to a consumption-based credit system effective June 1, 2026, with a preview period in May.
assertions.evidence: GitHub announced a shift to consumption-based fees. The switch comes with a revised multiplier table and a preview of bills during May before the switch at the beginning of June. Chief product officer Mario Rodriguez stated, 'Usage-based billing fixes that. It better aligns pricing with actual usage.'

assertions.claim: Anthropic's revenue run rate increased from $3 million last year to $47 billion currently, driven by a shift from seat-based pricing to usage-based pricing for AI agents.
assertions.source: AI Daily Brief host (citing industry data)
assertions.evidence: The difference between seat-based pricing and usage-based pricing is the difference between the $3 million run rate that Anthropic had last year and the $47 billion run rate that they're currently on.

assertions.claim: The 'token subsidy era' is ending, transitioning into a 'token scarcity era' where AI business models are shifting to charge for actual token consumption, fundamentally changing how value is captured and distributed.
assertions.evidence: If you've been listening to this show at all over the last few weeks, the number one most dominant and most important theme has been the shift from the token subsidy era to the token scarcity era where the business models are all shifting to sell people the tokens that they're actually consuming.

assertions.claim: Microsoft's per-user business models, including productivity, coding, and security, will transition to per-user and usage-based models.
assertions.evidence: The host quotes Satya Nadella: 'Any per user business of ours, whether it's productivity or coding or security, will become a per user and usage business.'

assertions.claim: Perplexity charges enterprises for 'Computer' on a usage-based model rather than a seat-based model, citing variable underlying costs for different task types such as video generation versus text memos.
assertions.evidence: Perplexity is charging enterprises on a usage-based model rather than a seat-based model... the rationale from the Perplexity team is that the underlying cost structure is so different depending on what type of task you're doing. Generating a video, for example, is going to cost a lot less than generating a text memo.

assertions.claim: Anthropic's annual revenue run rate surged from $30 billion to $47 billion by late May, driven primarily by high usage of Claude Code rather than new seat-based subscriptions.
assertions.evidence: Anthropic had this insane 80X surge that catapulted it to a $30 billion annual revenue run rate, which then jumped all the way up to $47 billion by late May. This was driven not by all sorts of new people paying for 20 or $200 a month Claude accounts, but an insane amount of usage of Claude code.
